analysis:
Examined the MiMoV26NativeLoadTransaction.swift changes. The only changed region is a test-only hook (mediaReservationRemovalHookForTesting, set at line 299, used in removeSettledMediaReservation at lines 1097-1110). The hook is read under the lock and invoked outside it, so there is no lock re-entrancy. The removal logic is unchanged: it still removes only when reservation.isFullyRetired and the map entry is identical. No change to retire(), the media reservation accounting, or the charge/credit paths. The hook is internal and has no production setter. It carries no request content, so it adds no data exposure. The ledger and availability behavior around A-018/TB-007 is unchanged.

Reviewed the new LoopExitThinkingContinuation.swift (added file, 233 lines). It holds back the engine's `length` terminal when the loop guard requested a thought exit. It then submits one continuation whose prompt is promptTokens + generated + exitTokens. The prompt is the same consumer's own data, re-submitted through the same bridge. Security-relevant observations:
- The continuation budget is bounded: min(outputBudget - completion - exitTokens, answerTokenLimit), and it is skipped below 256 tokens. This limits additional GPU work, but a re-prefill of the whole thought is extra compute per request (a bounded DoS/billing consideration for T-010/T-029, not a regression).
- Cancellation is ordered by Control (lock-protected). A cancel that loses to the start also calls cancelContinuation, so the in-flight work is stopped (T-010). onTermination cancels the task and the row.
- Errors are fail-closed with respect to encryption: this layer only forwards GenerationEvents, and the encryption of chunks stays downstream (T-008). Error strings from `submit` failures go only to the onOutcome/log path (`continuation refused: \(error)`), not to the client stream. Client-visible `.error(message)` is forwarded only after the client's cancel.
- Usage reporting sums the carried tokens and the continuation's tokens, so billing is consistent with the tokens produced.
- The prefix cache (T-041) is unchanged in kind. The continuation prompt shares the same prefix, so under the same cacheSalt scope it may hit the cache. No cross-account scope change is visible here.

Remaining integration questions, outside the supplied evidence: how EngineV2Bridge passes cacheSalt/account scope and the budget charge to the continuation submit closure, and whether waitForRowRelease is bounded. I found no concrete regression in the supplied code.
